item.title: Frontier's GoWild All You Can Fly pass is back with no blackout dates and earlier booking
item.description:
Source: The Points Guy
It's here! Frontier Airlines is now offering its GoWild All You Can Fly Pass for 2027, letting travelers take to the skies at a deep discount for an entire year (and potentially longer). Here are all the details. For a limited time, flyers can purchase a GoWild Pass good through 2027 for just $399. Members of the airline's Discount Den can score the pass for $349. While that's not quite as good as some offers we've seen in past years (but better than some in other years), it can add up to significant savings if you fly the airline a lot. You must be a Frontier Miles member to purchase one. Keep in mind that passholders pay $0.01 in airfare plus applicable taxes, fees and charges at the time of booking, so the pass gets you out of the regular airfare, but you're still on the hook for taxes and fees as well as other charges for things like optional seat selection and bags. While taxes on domestic legs are low, international ones can incur $60-$110 each way, depending on the destination. Multiple passholders can book travel at the same time, but you can't mix and match passholders with non-passholders on the same reservation. Likewise, different types of fares can be combined each way on itineraries as long as all passengers hold a valid GoWild Pass at the time of booking and the primary passenger holds a Discount Den membership if Discount Den fares are selected. One other big caveat: GoWild passes autorenew, so if you want to cancel when your current pass expires, you'll need to contact the airline to do so. Your renewal date will be stated in your confirmation email when purchasing the pass. Where can you fly? The GoWild Pass is valid for flights to over 100 destinations across Frontier's route network, including both domestic gateways and international cities in Mexico, the Caribbean and Central America. The airline's route network changes frequently, though, so stay on top of it to make sure your route will be in service when it's time to book. Travel begins after purchase (meaning as soon as today) and is available through Dec. 31, 2027, meaning potentially over a full year of flying. There are no blackout dates, like we've seen in some past instances, but on peak dates, you can expect to pay $59-$199 extra per segment. Peak dates for 2027 include: Here's the kicker: Standard bookings for eligible GoWild fares begin a day before departure for domestic flights and 10 days before departure for international flights. If your return flight is outside that window, then you'll have to try to make an additional booking when the window opens for that flight. If you do want to book more in advance than that, however, you can pay an additional charge to do so, though this can vary based on the date and the route. Also keep in mind that just because a seat is open on the flight you want does not mean it's eligible for a GoWild booking. You can earn Frontier Miles on the purchase of the pass as well as any extras, like seat assignments, bag fees or priority boarding that you purchase. If you hold elite status with Frontier, you are still eligible for your benefits, including free seats and bags, so that can be a great way to save on optional fees that non-elites have to pay. All-you-can-fly airline passes are a rarity these days and come with lots of limitations. Frontier Airlines' GoWild All You Can Fly Pass is no exception. Still, if you fly the airline a lot, have flexibility (and a bit of spontaneity) in your plans and don't need a ton of extra amenities like preferred seats or checked bags, these fares can be a good way to save a bit on flights you'd be taking anyway ... or perhaps some fun last-minute fares you wouldn't be able to take advantage of otherwise. item.title: IDEA: The Smarter Way Frequent Flyers Choose Travel Pillows
item.description:
Source: GoBackpacking
Ask any frequent flyer about their travel pillow, and you'll usually get a strong opinion because most people have tried several before finding one that works. It's rarely about brand loyalty; it's about trial and error, sore necks, and pillows that looked great online but slid off as soon as they fell asleep. After enough flights, experienced travelers stop picking pillows based on looks or price and start evaluating them like any gear they rely on repeatedly. That shift in approach is worth understanding before you buy your next one, especially if your last few pillows ended up unused in a bag. New travelers often buy the first neck pillow they see at an airport kiosk, thinking any support is better than none. After a few uncomfortable flights, most realize that's not true. A poorly shaped pillow can make things worse, forcing your neck into an unnatural angle. Frequent flyers learn to look past marketing claims and pay attention to structure, adjustability, and how a pillow performs in different seat types, not just how it looks in photos. What Seasoned Travelers Actually Look For The most common shift is moving away from soft, shapeless pillows to ones with defined structure that hold their form through hours of travel. A good travel pillow should keep its shape whether you're upright, leaning against a window, or changing positions on a long overnight flight. Adjustability matters too, since a pillow that fits a short domestic hop differently than an international red-eye is more useful than one built for a single scenario. This kind of practical, structure-first thinking is exactly what shaped Sarisun's approach to designing pillows meant for repeat travelers rather than occasional use. Comparing Options Without Getting Overwhelmed Someone flying once a year can usually get by with a basic design, while someone flying monthly benefits from investing in a pillow that holds up over repeated use without losing shape or support. Short flights call for something compact and easy to pack, while long-haul travelers should prioritize a pillow that fully supports the head throughout prolonged sleep, since the comfort stakes are higher over ten or twelve hours in the air. Travelers who stop cycling through pillows every few trips usually take time to think about their travel habits before buying, rather than grabbing whatever is convenient. Considering how often you fly, what kind of trips you take, and how much structure you need turns pillow shopping from a guessing game into a straightforward decision you likely won't repeat for years. Buying Once, Flying Comfortably for Years The difference between frequent flyers and occasional travelers isn't luck; it's that they've learned what matters in a travel pillow and stopped settling for less. By focusing on structure, adjustability, and fit for your travel habits, you can skip the years of trial and error most people go through. A thoughtful choice made once pays off on every trip that follows. This story was published in partnership with Sarisun.

item.title: INSTRUCTION: 14 tricks to getting the most value from your cruise vacations
item.description:
Source: The Points Guy
Squeezing the most value out of every dollar on a cruise is a top goal for most travelers. It doesn't matter if you're on a quick escape cruise from a local port or an exotic luxury cruise halfway around the globe, you never want to end it feeling like you should have gotten more for your money. Cruises are the ultimate all-inclusive vacation, with meals, transportation and entertainment included, and there is even more value-adds on board that you may have never thought to look for. The trick is to hone in on built-in value early, in the cruise shopping and purchasing stage, and then pay attention to every detail that might enhance your experience along the way. Here are 14 tricks to get the most possible value from any cruise you take. Watch your email for upgrade offers and advance-purchase deals on drinks, dining and Wi-Fi before you cruise It can feel like you’re bombarded with emails after you book a cruise, but some of them contain hidden treasure. Royal Caribbean, Celebrity, Princess, MSC and Virgin Voyages are among the cruise lines that use a bidding process to manage unsold cabins as the sailing date gets closer. Carnival Cruise Line offers upgrades without bidding. Pay attention to your email, and you might nab a nicer cabin for less than you’d pay by booking it outright. Emails also alert you to discounted packages or bundles for Wi-Fi, shore excursions, specialty dining, drinks and even spa treatments. Much of the same information can be found on the cruise planner on the cruise line's website, but unless you log in often, watch those emails for value-oriented offers. While it's tempting to always look at the newest (and often the biggest) ships, you may find that switching to an older or smaller ship, which may be just slightly less in demand, often helps squeeze more from your cruise budget without limiting your vacation fun. You can also save hundreds of dollars by opting for inside staterooms, rooms with partially blocked views or those with less-than-perfect locations on the ship. This even works within suite zones or exclusive ship-within-a-ship areas. My dermatologist recently confided that he always chooses an inside suite within the Yacht Club when he cruises with MSC; he gets all the VIP perks, including exclusive dining and entertainment venues, for thousands less than the suites with balconies. And don't rule out the cruise cabin guarantee option. Regardless of the cabin type, allowing the cruise line to select your stateroom is almost always the better value option than picking a specific room. While most lines sign you up for loyalty programs automatically after your first sailing, you might need to opt in. Some lines allow you to sign up even before your first cruise, giving you advance offers to entice you to go ahead and book that first cruise. Status matches between cruise lines are a huge bonus. MSC offers a status match with other cruise lines, hotel brands and tour operators. You can do this before your first booking and get Voyagers Club benefits on your first cruise with the line. These could be as simple as a welcome beverage or as elaborate as a complimentary tasting menu dinner. Ultra-luxury sister brand, Explora Journeys, offers a one-time status match with MSC and comparable luxury lines. Royal Caribbean, Celebrity and Silversea have an ongoing status match across the three sister brands. That means you can reap rewards on a luxury line by earning status on a mainstream brand. Similarly, Viking’s loyalty program spans its river, ocean and expedition arms. Once you’ve cruised with the line, you’ll get benefits fleetwide, even if you try out a different kind of ship. Some lines offer casino status matches with land- and sea-based casinos that might even earn you a free cruise. These often come with exceptions; your casino status on Carnival won't get you a free cruise on sister line Princess, but casino status on Celebrity might. And don't be afraid of free cruise certificates handed out by reputable casinos on land where you have status. They’re the real deal, often based on long-standing partnerships between the casino and cruise lines. The reverse is also true. I’ve never been to WinStar Casino in Oklahoma, but they send me offers of free hotel nights using postcards featuring the Carnival logo, with which I have casino status. While not every loyalty perk holds a huge value for you, little freebies definitely add up on vacation. For example, Carnival gives you a free 1.5-liter bottle of water on your second cruise. That's one less bottle you might have to buy. As you move up the loyalty ladder, cruise by cruise, the perks improve. For example, you may be eligible for free laundry, drinks and specialty dining the higher up you go. I once met a couple who were on a five-night Royal Caribbean cruise for the sole purpose of moving up to the top loyalty tier before going on a much longer cruise. The higher tier would give them free Wi-Fi and a handful of other valuable perks for the duration of their longer cruise. Often the onboard perks are loaded on your cabin keycard, but you might have to ask how to use them. For example, if you are entitled to a free bag of laundry at your loyalty level, nobody will hand you a bag and say, "Fill it up; it's free." It's up to you to know the perks you are entitled to and follow through on getting them. Amid the barrage of marketing messages for beverage packages of all sorts, it's easy to forget that certain beverages are included in your cruise fare. Every cruise ship offers standard drip coffee, water, iced tea, hot cocoa, punch or lemonade and a variety of tea bags free of charge. Milk and juice are available at breakfast. Look for self-serve stations at the buffet, or ask your server. Sodas are included on premium lines like Windstar, Oceania and Viking, as well as on luxury lines like Seabourn, Silversea and Regent Seven Seas Cruises. Disney Cruise Line also offers free soft drinks but only from the beverage dispensers by the pool. It's surprising how many free (or included) alcoholic drinks you can procure once on board a ship. I've been offered sparkling wine at art auctions, galley tours and captain's events. Royal Caribbean and Celebrity both have free drinks for the top three tiers of loyalty status. Celebrity Cruises offers free drinks for anyone gambling in the casino. Carnival and Virgin Voyages are among the lines offering free drinks to select gamblers based on their prior gambling history. You might be eligible for those, even if you only gamble on land. The cabin you book might come with valuable perks, so know what they are so you don’t miss out. For example, Celebrity’s AquaClass cabins come with not only thermal suite access and exclusive dining in the line’s health-forward restaurant called Blu, but also a choice of exercise equipment. Yoga mats are supposed to be in the closet when you board, but you'll have to ask for any of the other items listed on the menu provided. Suites on most lines come with extra perks like included drink packages and specialty dining. On certain ships, even some smaller suite categories come with exclusive dining rooms only for the occupants of those categories. The food in these exclusive eateries is often a step above the main dining room and not to be missed if you are staying in the entitled category. The same goes for suite lounge access. You generally find snack and beverage stations stocked with specialty treats you won’t find elsewhere on board, making it worthwhile to at least sneak a peek at the lounge offerings if you paid for a category that comes with access. The cost of going out to the movies these days makes a cruise movie night a big value. Now that most of us watch movies by streaming them at home, actually going to the movies is a treat in and of itself. Movie nights on a ship are a step above your local movie theater. You might enjoy films on a giant poolside screen while you float in the pool or relax on a lounge chair with bar servers bringing the drinks to you. Disney Cruise Line screens first-run films for free, with costumed characters in attendance. Many lines serve free popcorn wherever movies are being shown. If staying in for a movie night in your jammies sounds good, take advantage of free or pay-per-view movies on your cabin’s TV. Disney is among the cruise lines with popcorn on the room service menu. On a Silversea cruise, I once told our butler we were staying in for an evening movie. His immediate reply was, "Shall I pop some corn for you?" The answer, of course, was, "Yes, please." Splurge on entertainment without actually splurging Live music, comedy acts, magic shows and musical theater are luxuries you can pay dearly for on land — but all of those are available on cruise lines at no charge. The larger the ship, the more entertainment options you will have. Free live music is found daily in lounges, pool areas, atriums and on stage in the main auditorium. Audience participation game shows, sometimes raucous in nature, usually take over lounge space a few nights of the cruise. The main stage will have a show nightly, either song-and-dance revues featuring an onboard cast or guest magicians, musicians and comedians, some with TV credits to their name. Larger ships might have separate comedy club venues to keep the laughs flowing every night of the cruise, with both family-friendly and adults-only shows. Clubs on dry land where these same performers appear often charge a $30-40 cover. On a recent Carnival cruise, I estimate my visits to the comedy club alone would have cost me several hundred dollars. Some lines lean heavily into specialty performances. Look for ice skating, aquatic high-diving and dance shows on select Royal Caribbean ships and acrobatic performances on Virgin Voyages and MSC Cruises. Royal Caribbean and Norwegian Cruise Line both offer Broadway musicals, while Disney produces live musical performances based on its popular animated movies. With so much free entertainment that would certainly cost a family hundreds in ticket prices on land, you’ll get a ton of value from your cruise if you attend the shows that most appeal to you. When the night's entertainment winds down, it's time to dance the night away and go clubbing — and cruise ship clubs don’t have a cover. Big ships crank up the party vibe after the last show in the main theater, so you can make the most of every second you’re awake. Hop from dance parties on the pool deck to karaoke in smaller bar venues and even silent discos in the atrium to keep the fun going into the wee hours. Eating out and trying local restaurants are hallmarks of vacation, but you can blow your budget doing that on land. You can spend a lot on specialty restaurants on board, too, but pay attention to timing to get the most value out of the free dining on board. If you know you would enjoy steak and lobster, do a little research to figure out which night they will be served in the main dining room. You don’t want to find out too late that you booked a specialty restaurant on the same night you could have been eating surf and turf at no additional cost. Themed brunches and afternoon tea are also main dining room events you don’t want to miss. Looking beyond the buffet and main dining room might turn up surprising food choices you didn't even know were included in your cruise fare. Pool grills serving juicy hamburgers, specialty coffee shops with snacks and even sandwiches and healthy choice salads near the solarium are all yummy examples of freebies tucked away in spots you might not think to look. As for the specialty restaurants, those are generally still a bargain compared to a similar meal at a land-based restaurant. Carnival's Steakhouse is a good example. The cost is $52 per person. That sounds steep, but if you've priced a filet mignon in a nice restaurant lately, you'll know that $52 barely covers the steak. At Fahrenheit 555, you'll be treated to appetizers, sides and desserts, making the cover charge a vacation value. Book your Steakhouse dinner for the first night of a sailing, and Carnival will usually throw in a complimentary bottle of house wine. For lounging in your cabin, free or low-cost room service boosts your cruise value. My personal favorite (especially on sea days) is enjoying a "first breakfast" of coffee and croissants from room service before heading out for a more substantial second breakfast. Take advantage of free and low-cost fun on private islands Private island experiences provide an inexpensive break from paying for excursions in other ports. First things first, the beach is free. Use of the lounge chairs is free (not always the case at some vacation destinations). Swimming in the ocean and in some pools is free. Depending on the island, you might find hammocks, hiking trails, game and sports areas and interesting snorkeling spots. Rental equipment for snorkeling and other water activities is usually reasonably priced, but you can bring your own gear. The major private islands all have complimentary barbecue buffets and occasionally other food trucks or fast-casual offerings. As with specialty dining on the ship, even the up-charged food won’t cost as much as at a theme park or on the beach at a vacation destination. Relying on shore excursions offered by the cruise line is the easy way to plan your days in port. It also keeps you safe from becoming one of those pier-running late-comers at departure time. Those tours are not always the best value, however. Lower-priced reputable port tours may take a bit more research on your part, but can save hundreds of dollars. I recently enjoyed a 4-hour kayak tour in Ketchikan with pickup near the pier and guaranteed on-time return that I booked directly on the Ketchikan Kayak Company's website, which saved me roughly $60 per person compared to the similar tour offered by the ship. And don’t forget that skipping organized tours altogether can also net you an amazing day in port. If tours aren't your jam, or you just don’t want the scheduling hassle in every port, consider simply venturing out on your own in search of fun. If the town is walkable, start with that. Or consider renting a car or simply hiring a taxi driver. I've visited Cozumel dozens of times on cruise ships, but had never seen the far side of the island. Last fall, a group of friends and family rented two Jeeps online from a rental agency located walking distance from the pier. We had a marvelous time stopping wherever we wanted, including for an impromptu tequila tasting (for the non-drivers, of course). Whether you're talking about something as simple as miniature golf, basketball, pickleball or table tennis, or as elaborate as surf simulators and multideck dry slides, cruise lines often load their ships’ upper decks with free fun. As with all things on a cruise, certain activities come with a cost, but you’ll find plenty of fun that does not add to your cruise bill. On land, you typically need to pay to access waterslides, splash parks, rock climbing walls and adventure and zip lines, but on many cruises, these active onboard attractions come free. Certain activities might require reservations or specific attire (like closed-toe shoes), so check out the details in advance. Did you know that some cruise lines let you buy VIP packages pre-cruise for a bundle of preferential treatment similar to suite category perks? The real value of these programs lies in not paying for an expensive suite while enjoying extra perks as if you did. Royal Caribbean's The Key includes early boarding times, a welcome lunch, fast lane access to select onboard activities, premium theater seating, departure day perks and free internet access for each guest who purchases the package. Celebrity's Premium Access is a similar bundle. The combination of complimentary room service and Premium Wi-Fi for two devices makes this package a cruise value. Holland America's Club Orange includes a complimentary cabin upgrade when available, priority check-in, priority lines at Guest Services and Shore Excursion desks, bathrobes, an expanded room service menu, a complimentary glass of sparkling wine, exclusive events like behind-the-scenes tours and coffee chats with performers and even separate dining rooms on some ships. With a bit of strategy, the cabin upgrade alone can justify the cost of the Club Orange add-on. This works best in Oceanview and Verandah categories where you can choose an obstructed view cabin at a low cost, banking on the Club Orange upgrade to a full-view room. Carnival’s Faster to the Fun offers early cabin access, express luggage delivery and priority check-in and embarkation, shuttle boarding, dining reservations, Guest Services line and debarkation. Note that Carnival blocks access to FTTF for some loyalty guests, including some casino loyalty members, to avoid stacking of perks. Norwegian Cruise Line’s Priority Access includes priority security, check-in and boarding processes on embarkation day, plus skip-the-line tendering and debarkation, complimentary standard room service and a $50 spa discount on port days. Cruises come with so much value bundled into the cost of the fare that it can be easy to overlook all the goodies that aren't costing you anything extra. Adding value to your cruise vacation can be as simple as reading the daily planner or taking a walk around the ship to discover all the included attractions. Whether it’s free entertainment in your favorite lounge, a dance lesson or no-cost prime rib in the main dining room, all those onboard freebies and low-cost add-ons make it possible to get outsize value from your cruise vacation. item.title: SALES: 18 Family Resorts That Go Above and Beyond for Those With Babies and Toddlers
item.description:
Source: Condé Nast Traveler
I've traveled to some pretty far-flung places, but nothing could have prepared me for the logistical circus of vacationing with a baby. Four years and 30 countries later, my son Julian has taught me a thing or two about what makes a resort genuinely welcoming to its littlest guests. For starters, there’s a massive difference between a hotel that hands your kid a coloring book at check-in and one that has anticipated the thousands of little things that can make or break a family vacation. The best resorts for infants and toddlers also understand that keeping littles happy isn’t a one-size-fits-all proposition. A baby might need a quiet nursery and a reliable nanny; a three-year-old might be thrilled to feed goats on an Austrian farm, explore a Japanese forest, or make plaster casts of lion tracks in the Kalahari. And parents? Sometimes we just want to eat dinner without having to negotiate with a tiny inquisitor. That kind of thoughtfulness is what sets the properties on this list apart. I’ve seen it firsthand at more than half a dozen of them, where the greatest luxury wasn’t necessarily the thread count or the size of the swimming pool, but getting to enjoy a five-star vacation instead of merely financing one for your offspring. Read on for the best resorts for infants and toddlers. FAQ: What is the best destination to travel to with an infant and/or toddler? For a first trip with a baby or toddler, destinations with manageable flight times, reliable medical care, and resorts that minimize the logistical headaches of traveling with little ones are ideal. Florida, Mexico, and the Caribbean are excellent starting points, with direct flights from many US cities, and resorts that cater specifically to young children. Four Seasons Resort and Residences Anguilla is one standout, offering complimentary baby equipment, a zero-entry family pool, and a splash pad. For families ready to venture farther, Portugal's Algarve is another excellent choice, especially Martinhal Sagres, where supervised childcare starts at six months. In the Austrian Alps, Moar Gut goes a step further, welcoming infants as young as 30 days into its professionally staffed nursery. Are there any good all-inclusive resorts for infants and toddlers? Absolutely. Jean-Michel Cousteau Resort in Fiji is particularly impressive, with meals, activities, and dedicated nanny care included in the rate. Children under six are assigned two nannies who work opposite shifts, providing personalized care throughout the day and evening, while older children are paired with Fijian companions who guide them through age-appropriate activities. Closer to home, Grand Velas Riviera Nayarit in Mexico features gourmet dining, a baby concierge who arranges infant equipment and coordinates meals and childcare, and specialty purées for its youngest guests (babysitting costs extra). What resort in the US is best for families with infants and toddlers? The Breakers Palm Beach in Florida is hard to beat. Its private beach and zero-entry family pool are ideal for little swimmers, while a 4,500-square-foot playground and the Seaside Family Entertainment Center—with its dedicated Toddler Cove—give youngsters room to burn off energy. The hotel can also supply cribs, strollers, and bottle warmers, as well as childproof guest rooms upon request. Parents, meanwhile, get the restaurants, spa, and old-school Palm Beach glamour that have made The Breakers a fixture on luxury travel lists for generations. item.title: INSTRUCTION: A total solar eclipse, the real-life Tatooine and crowd-free Roman ruins: The ultimate 7-day Tunisia road trip
item.description:
Source: The Points Guy
American citizens do not need a visa to visit Tunisia for stays of 90 days or less, just a valid passport with at least six months’ validity and one blank page. Tunisia is about to have a big year. On the morning of Aug. 2, 2027, a total solar eclipse will cut a path across the central part of the North African nation, bringing several minutes of darkness to sites like the ancient Roman amphitheater in El Jem, the Great Mosque of Kairouan and the dramatic Sahara Desert dunes and canyons surrounding Tozeur. The latter will also draw “Star Wars” fans to many of the Tatooine filming locations to mark the franchise’s 50th anniversary of the movie’s release in 2027. The capital of Tunis isn’t in the path of totality, but any trip in 2027 should also include a stop in the picturesque cliffside village of Sidi Bou Said, which UNESCO recently added to its World Heritage list, joining other culturally significant sites like the Medina of Tunis and the Archaeological Site of Carthage. This 7-day itinerary covers a tour of Tunisia’s most important cultural and historic landmarks in a road trip from Tunis to Tozeur and back, plus tips for where to be during the 2027 eclipse and how to maximize the perks and benefits of the Chase Sapphire Reserve® (see rates and fees) along the way. Currently, there are no nonstop flights between the United States and Tunisia, so you’ll need to plan for at least one layover before connecting to Tunis-Carthage International Airport (TUN), the country’s largest airport. I flew to TUN on Air France via Paris-Charles de Gaulle Airport (CDG), since I’m loyal to the SkyTeam alliance and it offered the most frequent connections. However, if you’re loyal to another airline alliance, you can also find connections to TUN on Lufthansa via Frankfurt, ITA via Rome, Royal Air Maroc via Casablanca and Turkish Airlines via Istanbul. Chase Sapphire Reserve editor tip: When booking flights, check the Chase Travel℠ portal to see what routes and airlines are available to book using the Points Boost feature. I found several business-class fares offering the maximum Points Boost value of 2 cents per point. I ultimately transferred 142,000 Chase Ultimate Rewards points to Air France-KLM Flying Blue after finding an amazing round-trip business-class fare directly on the Air France website, yielding a value of 5.83 cents per mile. I landed in Tunis around 5 p.m. after a red-eye flight from New York and a relaxed connection in Paris. A pre-arranged car transfer whisked me to the Four Seasons Hotel Tunis, a luxury beachfront resort in the suburb of Gammarth, about 30 minutes from the airport. Upon arrival, staff greeted me warmly and took me directly to my upgraded Deluxe Sea-View Room for an in-room check-in. The spacious room had a balcony overlooking the Mediterranean, a walk-in closet and a marble bathroom with a separate tub and a shower. After a quick rinse, I wandered down to Blu, the hotel’s alfresco poolside restaurant, where I enjoyed a refreshing salad of a soft local cheese, tomatoes, onions and peppers served with a glass of Tunisian rosé. Since it was my first day in the country, the friendly staff made sure I tried some spicy Tunisian harissa, a smoky chili paste drizzled in olive oil that I sopped up with fluffy squares of focaccia. Chase Sapphire Reserve editor tip: Book the Four Seasons Hotel Tunis through The Edit to use one of the twice-annual, up-to-$250 credits toward prepaid hotel stays of two or more nights reserved through Chase Travel. By booking through The Edit, I also received other perks like complimentary hotel breakfast for two and up to $100 property credit, which I used for meals but could have used toward spa treatments like the ceremonial hammam experience, which comes out to approximately $100. Since I only had one full day in Tunis, I headed out bright and early for a private tour of the capital’s major sites, booked through Chase Travel with Didon Tours. My guide, Baligh, and a private driver picked me up for a full 8-hour day that included lunch and fascinating storytelling about the city’s ancient and modern history and politics. To beat the cruise groups and midday heat, we visited the ancient ruins of Carthage first, taking in the views from Byrsa Hill before heading down to the circular Punic port and the massive seaside complex of the Baths of Antoninus. From there, we drove to the charming blue-and-white village of Sidi Bou Said, Tunisia’s newest UNESCO World Heritage site, for fresh juice and almond cakes at Cafe des Delices and iconic views of the beach below. While we didn’t have much time to browse the cliffside town’s shops, I did pick up some handmade souvenirs at the ceramic store at 16 Rue Habib Thameur. For lunch, we stopped in the coastal suburb of Le Goulette at Restaurant La Victoire for a traditional Tunisian meal of brick à l’oeuf, a deep-fried pastry stuffed with egg, tuna and onion and a freshly grilled dorade fish served with rice and carrots. Next, we turned inland toward the western side of the city to visit the Bardo Museum, set in a former palace and home to the world’s largest collection of Roman mosaics. (Don’t miss the mosaic of the Roman poet Virgil, flanked by the muses of history and tragedy, as it’s considered to be the Mona Lisa of Tunisia.) Finally, we hit the medina of Tunis, where we visited the courtyard of the Zitouna Mosque and made a quick pass through the souk's meandering lanes before returning to the hotel for a much-deserved swim in the indoor pool and a nap before a quiet room-service dinner. Chase Sapphire Reserve editor tip: Earn 8 points per dollar spent on Chase Travel purchases, including activities and tours like the one I booked. Those with more time can add another day in Tunis and split this itinerary into two for a more relaxed pace in each location. Around midday, I returned to the airport to pick up a rental car from Avis and set the GPS to drive two hours south to Kairouan, a UNESCO-recognized city famous for its picturesque medina and Great Mosque, which dates to the 9th century AD. While Kairouan is considered one of the holy cities of Islam, film buffs may recognize it from “Raiders of the Lost Ark,” where it stood in for 1930s Cairo. It lies along the northern boundary of the 2027 solar eclipse’s path of totality. La Kasbah Hotel, booked via Chase Travel, provided a soft landing with its private parking lot, pool and strong air conditioning. The shops and sites in the medina tend to close in the late afternoon, so if you arrive after then, plan on a quiet night in the hotel, cooling off in the pool or lounging on woven rugs in its vintage café, drinking mint tea. Chase Sapphire Reserve editor tip: Pay for car rentals with Chase Sapphire Reserve to receive primary auto rental coverage (just be sure to decline the agency's collision insurance). Though I didn’t end up needing it, I had peace of mind knowing I was covered for up to $75,000 of theft or collision damage to the rental car. Having arrived the previous afternoon after the mosque closed, I went first thing the next morning to admire the column-lined courtyard and three-tiered minaret before the tour groups arrived. The ticket to the mosque also included admission to the nearby Sidi Abid el Ghariani Mausoleum, built in the Moorish style with black and white marble arches. A few doors down, I stopped by the former home of the governor of Kairouan, an ornately decorated mansion that now serves as a rug shop. While I wasn’t in the market for a carpet, I enjoyed the architecture and left with a handwoven scarf for 40 dinars ($14). After checking out, I hit the road again for the 4.5-hour drive south to Tozeur, a city in the heart of the Sahara Desert. Though I drove straight through, making brief stops at gas stations along the way, it’s also possible to break up the drive with stops at either the well-preserved archaeological site of Sbeitla or the Roman baths of Gafsa. Just be mindful of timing: I wouldn’t recommend driving at night. Though the roads are well-maintained, speed bumps are common and harder to spot after dark. Once in Tozeur, I checked into Dar Saida Beya, a traditional Tunisian guesthouse, booked through Chase Travel. After a long drive, I had a quiet evening to walk around and explore the nearby old town center. Chase Sapphire Reserve editor tip: Though the upscale Mora Sahara Tozeur resort west of town isn’t bookable via Chase Travel currently, it’s still possible to earn 4 points per dollar spent on direct hotel bookings made with the Chase Sapphire Reserve. The Atlas Mountains meet the salt flats and sands of the Sahara Desert in Tozeur, creating an otherworldly landscape that inspired many film directors. Most notably, the canyons and dunes around Tozeur served as the filming location for the desert planet of Tatooine in the “Star Wars” movies. The epic sci-fi series is celebrating the 50th anniversary of its release in 2027, and fans can experience the eclipse from here, since Tozeur falls along the southern boundary of the path of totality. I booked a 7-hour tour with Attractive Discoveries via Chase Travel to see everything the area had to offer. Before diving into the area’s cinematic legacy, my driver and guide, Firas, began the day at Chebika Oasis, where a 45-minute hike wound through the ruins of a former Berber village and down to the oasis and its waterfall. Our next stop was the Grand Canyon of Tunisia, Mides Canyon, roughly a mile from the Algerian border and featured in films like “The English Patient.” During the 30-minute hike along the dry riverbed, I spotted no fewer than six falcons diving in and out of the cliff face while hunting. To avoid the worst heat of the day, the tour included a break from 1 to 5 p.m., during which we stopped to pick some dates from my guide’s family’s oasis of palm trees. I also tried a makloub sandwich filled with chicken, cheese and harissa and took a short nap. At 5 p.m. on the dot, Firas picked me up again in his 4x4 to head out into the desert to watch the sunset over the dunes. Along our drive, we spotted a herd of camels, stopped to climb the Ong Jmal or “Camel’s Neck” rock formation and did some adrenaline-inducing 4x4 driving. We arrived at the remaining film sets that served as the desert trading post of Mos Espa in “The Phantom Menace” just before sunset. To cap off the day, we drank fresh mint tea with almonds — a local treat — and watched the sun set behind the dunes before heading back into town. Chase Sapphire Reserve editor tip: Put the card's up to $300 annual credit to work on travel purchases like the tour I booked. The credit is applied automatically to eligible purchases each account anniversary year. The biggest Star Wars fans may want to stay another day to visit other nearby filming locations, such as Sidi Bouhlel Canyon and the Lars family homestead exterior near the town of Nefta. Since I had another 4.5-hour drive ahead of me that day, I left around 11 a.m. to drive back north to the city of El Jem via Chott el Djerid. Before heading off across the massive salt lake, I filled up my gas tank and packed snacks for the long drive since there aren’t many places to stop in the first couple of hours. Built about 1,800 years ago, the Roman amphitheater of El Jem is roughly 70% the size of Rome’s amphitheater but has significantly fewer crowds and offers wide-open access to each level — even the underground level where animals were kept before they fought gladiators. After checking into Hotel Julius, booked through Chase Travel, I dropped my bags and took the five-minute walk to the amphitheater before it closed. The 20 dinar ($7) ticket includes entrance to both the amphitheater and the nearby El Jem Archaeological Museum on the same day. Since I arrived a little later in the afternoon, I went to the museum first thing the next morning and justified the extra $7 by spending a leisurely morning taking in the incredibly detailed mosaics without being rushed. El Jem falls within the path of totality for the 2027 solar eclipse, so history buffs may want to make this city their home base for the celestial event. Chase Sapphire Reserve editor tip: Tunisia is still a predominantly cash-based society, so it may be hard to find restaurants that accept cards. I couldn’t earn 3 points per dollar spent on dining worldwide with my Chase Sapphire Reserve in El Jem, but the two fricassee (fried dough buns stuffed with egg, tuna, potato and harissa) I ordered at a street food stall on the way back from the amphitheater only cost 7 cents total (yes, really), so I wasn’t worried about missing out on too many points. After checking out the museum, I loaded up my rental car one last time for the two-hour drive back to Tunis. Those with more time and desire to sit on the beach than I did could easily add a day or two in the coastal town of Hammamet, which sits about two-thirds of the way back to Tunis from El Jem. Once I handed off my rental car keys at the airport, I met the taxi driver I had prearranged with my final hotel, Dar Ben Gacem, a traditional guesthouse in the Tunis medina. Since my tour of Tunis at the beginning of the trip only included a brief visit to the medina, I was glad to have the rest of the afternoon and evening to poke around the shops and alleys of the historic city center and do some final souvenir shopping before flying home the next day. Keep in mind that most stalls in the medina are open from around 8 a.m. to 5 p.m., with more closed on Fridays and Sundays, so plan your visit accordingly. (Plus, many restaurants are closed for dinner on Sunday nights as well.) Though some flights depart in the evening, I opted to take a connecting flight back to Paris in the morning and stay an extra night to avoid a rushed final day. During my week-long road trip, I explored Tunisia’s ancient ruins, UNESCO-recognized Islamic architecture and otherworldly desert landscapes, many of which lie in the path of totality of the 2027 solar eclipse. Booking through Chase Travel maximized my Ultimate Rewards earnings, while the card benefits helped offset travel expenses along the way, like the $300 annual travel credit on tours, The Edit perks and $250 statement credit at the Four Seasons and primary rental car coverage through Avis. When I returned to New York, I was glad I had enrolled in Global Entry before my trip. The Sapphire Reserve's $120 Global Entry application fee statement credit helped offset the cost, and the program made reentering the U.S. much easier.

item.title: IDEA: Where to go in 2027
item.description:
Source: The Points Guy
Epic celestial events and ancient landmarks with no galaxy far, far away required. Curated annually by TPG’s team of travel experts, this year’s Where to Go list highlights particularly exciting moments happening across the globe in 2027, including hotly anticipated and fabulous new hotels, milestone museum openings, travel-worthy celestial events, new UNESCO designations, new flight routes, major sporting events and so much more. And for 2027, we’ve pulled out all the stops: Below, you can explore our new interactive map displaying the 22 destinations that earned a spot on our list. Now more than ever, exploring new and familiar destinations fosters curiosity, connectedness, and, perhaps most importantly, compassion. It’s time to put those hard-earned points and miles toward your dream trip — and we’ve got just the ticket. Caribbean luxury that rewards every dollar you spend. Best in July through August + December through March New sightseeing trains and upscale points hotels make Japan’s stunning northern island even more alluring in 2027. For those who want to experience Hokkaido’s beautiful countryside by train, Hokkaido Railway Company will debut two scenic tourist trains in 2027: the Red Star luxury train in February, when the region is blanketed in Hokkaido’s signature fluffy snow, and the Blue Star premium class train in June, just in time for Hokkaido’s lavender season. And for skiers and snowboarders who are looking to experience Hokkaido’s incredible winter sports scene, Moxy Niseko will debut in late 2026, just in time for the start of ski season. Other exciting Niseko openings to look forward to in the coming years include Six Senses Niseko and an Aman property. In nearby Sapporo, new and forthcoming points hotels are plentiful, too: 2025 saw the opening of the InterContinental Sapporo, and both Hyatt Centric and Fairmont are planned for 2027 into 2028. -Ellie Nan Storck World-class dining and hotels to help fans refuel between Women’s World Cup matches. One of the most accessible host cities of the Women’s World Cup is also among the most captivating. Beyond the pitch, visitors can experience the city’s dining renaissance, the long-awaited Museum of Image and Sound and the one of the oldest national history museums in the Americas, recently reopened after a 2018 fire. Plus, Rio (and nearby Maricá) is the midst of a luxury hotel boom, with exciting points properties opening over the coming years. December will bring the opening of Accor’s Sofitel Rio de Janeiro Ipanema, and over the next few years, Marriott will debut an eco-luxe Ritz Carlton Reserve and an all-inclusive JW Marriott in Maricá. -Rachel Craft Best in March through May + October through November A perennial favorite is experiencing a luxury hotel boom. Mexico’s massive capital never lacked excellent hotel options, but a recent slate of renovations and openings has us more excited than ever to revisit the city. The St. Regis Mexico City completed a multimillion dollar renovation with Frida Kahlo-inspired design elements in Sept. 2026. Hyatt loyalists can look forward to the February opening of the colorful new Standard Hotel in the Tabacalera neighborhood, followed by the April debut of the luxe Park Hyatt in Polanco. Other upcoming projects to look forward to include a Mama Shelter (part of the ALL Accor hotel loyalty program) in the heart of Roma Norte, set to open by the end of 2026, as well as Pendry Mexico City and Rosewood Mexico City, both planned for 2027. -Lyndsey Matthews The perfect mix of new luxury hotels, a distinct wine scene and endless opportunities to get outside. In the Texas Hill Country, charming towns steeped in German culture are surrounded by award-winning wineries, idyllic swimming holes and Main Streets packed with restaurants, shops and some of the friendliest people in the Lone Star State. Near Fredericksburg, the epicenter of the Hill Country’s must-visit charm, Waldorf Astoria is opening its first Texas property, while Aman has plans for a secluded ranch retreat of its own. Add mouthwatering barbecue, legendary live music, popular rivers to float and an expanding Austin-Bergstrom International Airport (AUS), and there are more reasons than ever to head for the hills. -Tanner Saunders Rich in natural beauty, this coastal California town is ready to step into the spotlight. Wellness travelers, adventure travelers and everyone in between will fall for this sleepy coastal enclave along the northern California coast. Unwind at Marriott Bonvoy’s newest adventure lodge after exploring the recently opened Great Redwood Trail or sampling the latest additions to the town’s renowned sustainable food and wine scene. And thanks to nonstop flights from Alaska Airlines and Southwest and $20 million in roadwork funding, Mendocino is easier than ever to reach. -Rachel Craft Experience a quieter side of India in one of the world’s lushest biodiversity hotspots Like many of the best places, it can take a lot of time and effort to get to Coorg, a hill station in India’s verdant, biodiverse Western Ghats. But it is well worth it to see this little-visited region rife with endemic wildlife including elephants, leopards and myriad avian species. Spend your days sampling world-class coffee at the area’s many plantations, hiking the misty mountain trails and recentering yourself with immersive multiday Ayurvedic wellness programs at the stunning new Leela Coorg Forest Sanctuary. -Eric Rosen In anticipation of hosting the EXPO 2027, the Serbian capital is undergoing a major glow-up From May 15 to Aug.15, the Serbian capital will host a specialized world exposition with 140-plus countries gathering to showcase innovations in architecture and design. In anticipation of the event, Belgrade is debuting several major projects of its own, including a Nikola Tesla Museum designed by Zaha Hadid Architects. The former main railway station will become the new permanent home of the Historical Museum of Serbia, while the Museum of the City of Belgrade and the Museum of Natural History Belgrade will also open in new facilities. Finally, the Aeronautical Museum of Belgrade will also complete a modernization project in 2027. To accommodate the influx of visitors, the city already opened a St. Regis in 2024, while the InterContinental Belgrade is accepting reservations from next March, with a Ritz-Carlton also anticipated to open, too. -Lyndsey Matthews Best in May through June, September through October A pair of new destination-worthy hotels, both bookable with points. Hyatt and Marriott will both debut luxury properties in Detroit come 2027. Hilton’s new hotel, the NoMad Detroit, will open inside the historic Michigan Grand Central Station, a once-abandoned Beaux-Arts landmark restored by Ford. Later in the year, the Marriott Edition will open as part of a ground-up development, bringing downtown Detroit its first five-star hotel. -Carly Helfand A new film festival is just one facet of this art-meets-outdoors jewel. Between hosting its first Sundance Film Festival and celebrating 50 years of the iconic Pearl Street Mall, Colorado’s trendy cultural hub is going all out. Visitors can also look forward to new dining concepts from Michelin-recognized chefs, new interactive art labs and easy access to new Rocky Mountain hiking trails. An hour away, Denver International Airport (DEN) is expanding to accommodate increased traffic from United, Southwest and even Delta. -Rachel Craft Jungle-covered islands and seas teeming with marine life beckon explorers beyond the bright lights of Bali. Cruise companies are lining up new expeditions to explore the Indonesian archipelago’s untouched corners, including a seven-day sailing aboard Uniworld’s Aqua Blu that will stop in Komodo National Park and the Spice Islands, Ponant’s team-up with Smithsonian Journeys on a 15-day jaunt around the Maluku islands among other ports of call and specialized dive-focused sailings in wild West Papua, reef-rich Raja Ampat and untamed Borneo from Swan Hellenic and Noble Caledonia. It’s the best way to experience regions of the Indonesian archipelago most folks never see. -Eric Rosen Australia’s first Michelin Guide, new luxury hotels and experiences, nonstop access from the U.S. and an extraordinary mix of world-class wine, wildlife and wilderness make 2027 South Australia’s moment on the global stage. Australia’s first Michelin Guide and United’s nonstop San Francisco-Adelaide flight are putting South Australia within easier reach — and on the global culinary map, too. A significant transformation of Adelaide Central Market, Australia’s first Treehouse Hotel and new luxury stays are adding fresh reasons to visit, alongside the Barossa and McLaren Vale wine regions and the wildlife and rugged beauty of Kangaroo Island. -Tanner Saunders Best in April through June, September through October Natural wonders and a burgeoning culture scene without the crowds. Though Kazakhstan first made a name for itself as a nature travel destination, this Eurasian country wants the world to know there’s more to it than its glorious landscapes. Travelers can enjoy a new art museum and immersive ethno-village in the cultural capital of Almaty, check into new hotels in the Burabay resort region or combine natural and cultural wonders at the newly inscribed Mangystau Rock Mosques UNESCO World Heritage Site. With plans to launch the first-ever direct flight from the U.S. in 2027, this hidden gem may not stay hidden for long. -Rachel Craft Two iconic cultural institutions, back and better than ever. The Pergamon Museum will reopen in June after a multi-year renovation, debuting a fully redesigned Museum of Islamic Art and making the Pergamon Altar accessible for the first time in more than a decade. Later in the year, the Bauhaus Archive will reopen after extensive renovations with a new annex building. With nonstop options from the U.S. on United, Delta and Lufthansa — and strong Hilton and Marriott footprints downtown — early points bookings are a smart play for visiting Berlin in 2027. -Carly Helfand Best in April through June, September through November Experience a slower type of journey that has captivated travelers for over 1,000 years. Special events will be taking place at waystations along this ancient pilgrimage trail throughout the Holy Year of 2027. Among the highlights are braving the wine battle in Haro at the end of June, or attending St. James’s Feast Day on July 25 in Santiago de Compostela, where you can see the famous swinging of the Botafumeiro silver incense burner and attend an awe-inspiring mass in the Praza do Obradoiro. Aside from a full calendar of culinary festivals and lively concerts in Santiago, you can take in quieter stretches of the trail among the forested peaks of Cantabria and the vineyards of Rioja. -Eric Rosen Astrotourism investments and a highly anticipated points hotel transformation. Dramatic coastal landscapes, the new Atlantic Canada UNESCO Tourism Corridor and the re-opening of the transformed The Algonquin Resort St. Andrews by-the-Sea, Autograph Collection resort make a compelling case for a 2027 visit to New Brunswick. Specifically, we’re excited to check out the Bay of Fundy Dark Sky Corridor that’s set to open in 2027 — a 137-mile stretch that could be the densest cluster of dark-sky and observatory areas on the planet. A stargazer’s dream come true. -Madison Blancaflor A burgeoning wine scene, an exciting UNESCO designation and outdoor attractions aplenty give one of BC’s prettiest regions a well deserved moment in the spotlight With plenty of sunny days and a generally milder climate than the rest of British Columbia, the Okanagan Valley is becoming an increasingly compelling alternative to larger wine regions; oenophiles can look forward to sipping wines from smaller producers (small but mighty; there are over 200) in a community-forward and breathtaking lakeside setting. Those in search of a city getaway should head to Kelowna, the valley’s largest metropolis set along the breezy shorelines of Okanagan Lake, where a major culinary moment is afoot. Recently designated Canada’s first UNESCO Creative City of Gastronomy — a designation that honors not only the city’s agricultural innovation and culinary creativity, but the traditional foodways and land stewardship of the indigenous Syilx people — Kelowna offers a fast-growing restaurant scene (many with a sustainable, farm-to-table focus) and its own array of impressive wineries. -Ellie Nan Storck Travelers can look forward to fully restored access to Denali Park Road for the first time in six years With more access now than ever, thanks to both recently expanded Alaska Airlines routes to nearby Fairbanks International Airport (FAI) and the very exciting full reopening of Denali Park Road for the summer season, 2027 is the year to plan an epic trip to Denali National Park. And the fun doesn’t stop there — Holland America, celebrating 80 years of Alaskan exploration, will complete a massive transformation of Holland America Denali Lodge, debuting 72 new guest rooms, updated public spaces and refreshed dining programs. Beyond the park, the Alaska Railroad — which celebrated its centennial in 2023 — is a great way travelers can experience a legendary scenic trip between Anchorage, Talkeetna, Denali and Fairbanks. -Ellie Nan Storck Expanded access from the U.S. and newly awarded Michelin key hotel recognition. Delta is adding a new nonstop route from L.A. to Manila and Philippine Airlines is joining the oneworld alliance, making a trip to the gorgeous islands of The Philippines easier than ever in 2027. Head to the islands early in the year for milder temperatures, vibrant festivals and the chance to ethically swim with majestic whale sharks in Donsol, Sorsogon. Nature lovers and beach loungers can also enjoy luxury properties like the Raffles Makati and the forthcoming Mandarin Oriental Makati, Manila (opening in December) or use points to book the brand new AC Hotel by Marriott Manila. -Madison Blancaflor Best in June through September, January through March These lush African islands are ready for their moment in the sun. Thanks to its pristine tropical forests and rare wildlife species, in 2025 São Tomé and Principe became the first country in the world whose entire territory, both land and sea, was designated as a UNESCO biosphere reserve. This past year, the country scored a second UNESCO designation for its historical roças, or colonial agricultural estates, making São Tomé and Principe ripe for discovery. Even better — you can use your Star Alliance points and miles to fly direct from Lisbon on TAP and Hilton points can set you up for a beachy stay at the luxurious Sundy Praia – Principe Collection. -Eric Rosen Best in April through May, September through October For travelers ready to venture beyond familiar South American tourism destinations and experience a different side of the continent. Travelers who have already visited Peru, Brazil, Argentina and other South American hot spots can find something different in the continent’s less-visited interior. Don’t go expecting a long list of world-famous sights or extensive tourism infrastructure. Instead, go for a quieter, slower-paced trip shaped by Indigenous Guaraní culture and landscapes ranging from the vast Chaco lowlands to the biodiverse remnants of the Atlantic Forest along the Paraná River. New attractions are adding reasons to visit: MUVA Museo Viedma, a museum exploring Paraguay’s Guaraní-Jesuit heritage through murals by artist Manuel Viedma, opened in Misiones in May 2026, and Asunción’s Museo de Ciencias plans to open a planetarium in 2028. -Mackenzie Roche Book flights, hotels and activities through Chase Travel℠ for the Cayman Islands, Tunisia and more, and earn points while you’re planning your next adventure.

item.title: The 50 Best Vineyards for 2026 revealed: a German vineyard tops the list, with only one UK entry
item.description:
Source: Condé Nast Traveler UK
The 50 Best Vineyards for 2026 (formerly The World's 50 Best Vineyards) have been unveiled – an annual dispatch that doubles as a passport to the planet’s most seductive wine destinations. For oenophiles, tasting-trail devotees and anyone who has daydreamed about wandering sun-struck estates with a glass in hand, this is the ultimate pilgrimage list. This year, it looks like wine fans may be making their way to Germany's dreamy Rheingau region. The 2026 awards were announced at a ceremony at Santiago's Viña Don Melchor, a sprawling vineyard at the foot of the Chilean Andes, after Vik, the hilltop estate in Chile's Millahue, was named The World’s Best Vineyard last year. Any estate that has once claimed the No.1 spot is retired into the Hall of Fame, so Vik joins luminaries such as Catena Zapata, Zuccardi Valle de Uco and Antinori nel Chianti Classico. Only one UK vineyard made this year's top 50 list. Gusbourne in Kent came in at No. 24, climbing four positions up from last year. Just an hour outside of London, this winery stretches across a 150-acre estate where you'll find some of the country's most awarded collection of sparkling wines. We saw a few more English vineyards make it into this year's 51-100 list, though, all in Sussex: Nyetimber (No. 53), Leonardslee Family Vineyards (No. 71) and Ridgeview (No. 92). Which vineyard was named the Best in the World for 2026? Just like we saw in this year's 50 Best Restaurants list, it was last year's number two that nabbed the top spot for 2026. Schloss Johannisberg in Germany's Rheingau region is now officially the Best Vineyard in the World. Considered the world's oldest Riesling vineyard, it's been a long time coming for Schloss Johannisberg who've been in the winemaking game since 1720. Set in a beautiful palace-topped estate perched above the Rhine, a Riesling tour here means wandering around the historic grounds and visiting the underground Bibliotheca Subterranea, a wine cellar nine metres deep and carved into Taunus quartzite. As for the full list, here's who made the top 50 vineyards this year: 10. Durigutti Family Winemakers, Mendoza 12. Pago de Carraovejas, Ribera del Duero 27. Jordan Vineyard & Winery, Alexander Valley 29. William Chris Vineyards, Texas Hill Country What are the best vineyards on each continent? The 2026 awards also highlighted the top vineyard on each continent. Schloss Johannisberg is The Best Vineyard in Europe, of course. Vasse Felix (No.17) in Australia's Margaret River is The Best Vineyard in Australasia. Montes (No.3) in Chile's Colchagua Valley claims The Best Vineyard in South America, as South Africa's Creation (No. 5) is awarded The Best Vineyard in Africa. In California's Sonoma County, Jordan Vineyard & Winery (No.27) earns the title of The Best Vineyard in North America, while Lebanon's Château Kefraya wins The Best Vineyard in the Middle East. Which vineyards ranked 51-100 in The 50 Best Vineyards in 2026? 95. Azienda Agricola Arianna Occhipinti, Sicily 93. Sandeman Quinta do Seixo, Douro Valley 90. Domaine Henri Bourgeois, Loire Valley 87. Champagne Laurent Perrier, Champagne 81. Midalidare Estate, Thracian Lowlands 71. Leonardslee Family Vineyards, Sussex 69. Mission Hill Family Estate, Okanagan Valley 67. Ridge Vineyards (Monte Bello), Santa Clara 66. Familia Torres (Pacs Del Penedès), Penedès 57. Château & Village Castigno, Languedoc 51. Château & Domaine de Briante, Beaujolais How are The World's 50 Best Vineyards chosen? As with its culinary siblings – The World’s 50 Best Restaurants, Bars and Hotels – the list is curated by the global academy: a sprawling network of 700 wine authorities, travel writers and industry insiders, all voting anonymously to preserve integrity. The world is split into 20 regions, each headed up by an acknowledged expert as its Academy Chair. Each region is responsible for recruiting 36 wine and travel professionals. Each member of the Voting Academy must vote for seven vineyards. There is no pre-determined checklist of criteria or predefined list to choose from – each vote is a nomination for a vineyard experience open to the public that they deem to be truly among the best in the world.

item.title: Alaska Airlines adds 4 new cities to its map amid broader route shakeup
item.description:
Source: The Points Guy
Alaska Airlines will add four new destinations across the U.S. to its map. But the additions come at a cost: The carrier has discontinued four recently added routes from its hub at Portland International Airport (PDX) in Oregon. As airline executives say, every route has to earn its place financially in a carrier’s network. As for the four new destinations, Alaska will serve each of those with one daily flight from its Seattle-Tacoma International Airport (SEA) base. The additions are: - Charlotte Douglas International Airport (CLT) on a Boeing 737-900ER starting June 10, 2027 - Des Moines International Airport (DSM) on an Embraer E175 starting June 24, 2027 - Jacksonville International Airport (JAX) on a 737-900ER starting June 24, 2027 - Norfolk International Airport (ORF) on a 737-900ER starting June 10, 2027 The carrier will also add a new nonstop from SEA to Guadalajara International Airport (GDL) in Mexico. Alaska will offer three weekly flights on Thursdays, Fridays and Saturdays with a 737-800 from March 18, 2027 through Aug. 9, 2027. Alaska currently serves GDL from Los Angeles International Airport (LAX) and San Jose Mineta International Airport (SJC) in California's Bay Area, schedule data from aviation analytics firm Cirium shows. The Seattle growth comes as Alaska builds its intercontinental offerings from the Pacific Northwest city. After launching its first long-haul flights in 2025 after its merger with Hawaiian Airlines, Alaska is building out a network of at least 15 intercontinental routes from SEA by 2030. Alaska plans to grow its schedule by about 4% year-over-year in 2027, with the majority in long-haul international additions. PDX, Alaska’s wunderkind hub of recent years, is losing four recently added routes. The airline will not resume seasonal service in 2027 to: - Baltimore/Washington International Thurgood Marshall Airport (BWI) - Louis Armstrong New Orleans International Airport (MSY) - St. Louis Lambert International Airport (STL) Alaska continues to serve all four destinations from one of its other hubs. PDX remains one of Alaska’s fastest-growing hubs as the airline shifts connections to the Oregon city. The carrier's seats at the airport are set to increase 12% in the first half of 2027 compared to this year after a 17% increase during the same period in 2026, Cirium schedules show. "Portland is a story of focused smart growth that improves utility, strengthens the local franchise and captures the right traffic flows," Andrew Harrison, the chief commercial officer at Alaska, said in September. "[PDX] proves that Seattle and Portland are stronger together, allowing us to serve more customers, connect more traffic and improve the efficiency of our Pacific Northwest network." As part of its PDX growth, Alaska Airlines opened a new, $18 million lounge at the airport in June. Related reading:

item.title: JSX expands semi-private jet service in New York with new Dallas route
item.description:
Source: The Points Guy
JSX, the boutique semi-private flight operator, is launching a new daily route between New York City and Dallas, the company announced this week. The new service will fly to Dallas Love Field (DAL) starting on Feb. 17, with one daily flight in each direction. JSX did not immediately disclose which airport in New York it plans to fly from. JSX typically flies to New York’s Teterboro Airport (TEB) and Westchester County Airport (HPN), although various restrictions set by the Port Authority of New York and New Jersey mean that JSX cannot publicly promote TEB as a destination. Those restrictions limit JSX to only selling those New York flights to members of its free Club JSX program, which offers rewards and has no minimum spending or flying requirements. When logged into that platform, the new route is currently bookable from TEB. The carrier will use its Embraer E145 aircraft on the route, which can seat up to 30 passengers in a 1-1 configuration. Introductory fares start at $799 one-way. "New York City and Dallas are two of America's most influential business and cultural centers, and we believe traveling between them should be as seamless as the opportunities that connect them,” Alex Wilcox, CEO of JSX, said in a statement. "With this new daily service, we're bringing the simplicity, comfort, and convenience of JSX to one of the country's most important travel corridors." The new flight to Dallas is JSX second New York City expansion in as many weeks; the carrier announced new flights between New York and Boston earlier this month. The Dallas route is the company's fifth route from New York — aside from Boston, JSX flies from New York to Fort Lauderdale Executive Airport (FXE); Miami-Opa Locka Executive Airport (OPF); Naples Airport (APF); and President Donald J. Trump International Airport (DJT), formerly known as Palm Beach International, all in Florida. JSX operates out of 30 airports across the U.S. and Mexico and functions as a public charter service, rather than a formal "airline." This lets the carrier's flights work more like private ones — although anyone can buy a ticket, the flights use posh private Fixed-Base Operators (FBOs) instead of public airport terminals. That allows passengers to venture from curb to seat in just 20 minutes. The flight experience itself is equally luxurious with no middle seats, lots of legroom, Starlink Wi-Fi, complimentary snacks and drinks and checked luggage that’s returned right at the side of the plane. The carrier has a fleet of 56 ERJ-family jets and 4 ATR 42-600 turboprop aircraft. Overall, the service pitches the idea of private jet convenience for a fraction of the cost. JSX passengers used to bypass security screening, like passengers on most private flights. In 2025, the carrier implemented its own in-house screening process to address security concerns. item.title: INSTRUCTION: Red-Wine-Braised Short Ribs
item.description:
Source: Bon Appétit
These red-wine-braised short ribs have fans. “This has been my go-to recipe for short ribs for as long as I can remember,” says one commenter. “It never fails.” It’s the kind of special-occasion dish you make once and return to forever. Flavor builds in layers: The bone-in beef is browned, then the onions, carrots, and celery cook in its drippings. A full bottle of dry red wine reduces by half before the broth goes in; a whole head of garlic and plenty of fresh herbs round out the braise. After that, a few hours in the oven turn the meat fall-off-the-bone tender. Even better: You can make the ribs a day ahead, leaving little to do before dinner but reheat them. Serve over mashed potatoes, soft polenta, or wide egg noodles to soak up every drop of the rich sauce. What kind of short ribs should I buy? Look for meaty, bone-in English-cut short ribs, with a single rib bone beneath each piece of meat. Ask your butcher to cut them crosswise into 2" lengths—you’re not expected to saw through the bones at home. Avoid the thin strips sold for grilling. What’s the best wine for braised short ribs? Choose a dry red wine you’d enjoy drinking. Cabernet Sauvignon is the recipe’s first choice, but Merlot or a Rhône-style red also fits the bill. There’s no need to splurge; save your special bottle for the table. Do I have to strain the vegetables? For the smooth sauce intended here, yes. The vegetables flavor the braising liquid, and straining removes them along with the herb stems, bay leaves, and garlic skins. For a more rustic approach, pluck out the herbs and garlic skins (leave the cloves behind) and use an immersion blender to purée the cooked vegetables into the sauce. How do I know when short ribs are done? Start checking after 2 hours in the oven. A fork should slide into the meat easily, and a gentle twist should pull it apart. If the meat still resists, keep braising. The listed cooking time is a guide, not a hard stop. Can I make these short ribs ahead, and how should I reheat them? Yes. Finish cooking the ribs and strain the sauce, then refrigerate the ribs with their sauce in shallow containers within 2 hours of cooking. The next day, lift off the hardened fat. Transfer the ribs and sauce to an ovenproof pot or baking dish, cover, and reheat in a 350° oven until hot throughout—the meat should reach 165° in the center. Save recipes and plan every week with confidence. Download the app Try this recipe with this expert pick from the Bon Appétit Wine Shop. - Staub Enameled Cast Iron Round Dutch Oven 7-Qt. $300 $286 At Amazon Need to make a substitution? - Step 1Preheat oven to 350°. Season 5 lb. bone-in beef short ribs, cut crosswise into 2" pieces by your butcher, with kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper. Heat 3 Tbsp. vegetable oil in a large Dutch oven or other heavy pot over medium-high. Working in 2 batches, cook short ribs, turning occasionally, until browned on all sides, about 8 minutes per batch. Transfer to a plate. Pour off all but 3 Tbsp. drippings from pot. Step 2Cook 3 medium onions, chopped, 3 medium carrots, peeled, chopped, and 2 celery stalks, chopped, in same pot over medium-high heat, stirring often, until onions are browned, about 5 minutes. Add 3 Tbsp. all-purpose flour and 1 Tbsp. tomato paste and cook, stirring constantly, until combined and deep red, 2–3 minutes. Step 3Stir in one 750-ml bottle dry red wine (preferably Cabernet Sauvignon), then add short ribs along with any juices that have accumulated on the plate. Bring to a boil; reduce heat to medium and simmer until wine is reduced by half, about 25 minutes. Add 1 head of garlic, halved crosswise, 10 sprigs parsley, 8 sprigs thyme, 4 sprigs oregano, 2 sprigs rosemary, and 2 fresh or dried bay leaves; stir in 4 cups low-sodium beef broth. Bring to a boil, cover, and transfer pot to oven. Braise until short ribs are tender, 2–2½ hours. Step 4Uncover pot and transfer short ribs to a platter. Strain sauce through a fine-mesh sieve into a heatproof measuring glass; spoon fat from surface and discard. Season sauce with salt and pepper. Arrange ribs in shallow bowls, over mashed potatoes if desired, and spoon sauce over.
